clue.text: Pick scruffy lovelorn Rumpole to inspire court

definitions.note: a plectrum is the pick used to pluck a guitar's strings

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the jumbled letters take the court abbreviation inside them
something scruffy is messed about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
read as love (O, the zero score) plus lorn (bereft), so the name loses its O

parts.note: the barrister in John Mortimer's stories, taken as written

explanation.surface: A dishevelled, lovesick Rumpole picks a fight to stir up the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lovelorn' removes O (love) from RUMPOLE to leave RUMPLE; 'scruffy' rearranges that into PLE...RUM, and 'to inspire' breathes CT into the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A plectrum is the small flat tool a guitarist strikes strings with, commonly called a pick.

clue.text: Foresight of French invading region

indicators.note: invading means entering, so the French word goes inside the region

parts.note: a province is a region of a country
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Showing foresight, the French invaded a region.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence can mean prudent foresight or provision for the future, as well as divine care.

clue.text: Picked up second person's stock item

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: you is the second-person pronoun; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: Someone collected the second person's item from the stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Stock here is livestock, of which a female sheep is one item.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewe is a female sheep, one animal among a farm's livestock.

clue.text: Strict rule: radio has to impress Yankee

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the letter goes inside the radio word

parts.note: tranny is old British slang for a transistor radio
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Harsh regulations demand a radio broadcast to impress Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Tranny is dated British slang for a transistor radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranny is cruel, oppressive government, a harsh and strict form of rule.

clue.text: A foreign assassin went ahead without scruples

parts.note: un is a in French
Gavrilo Princip assassinated Archduke Franz Ferdinand in 1914
led means went in front

explanation.surface: A foreign killer pressed on without any scruples.
explanation.walkthrough: Princip is the Bosnian Serb assassin whose shots at Sarajevo triggered the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unprincipled lacks moral standards and acts with no conscience.

clue.text: Stars host introduction to solemn prayer

indicators.note: to host is to take in a guest, so the constellation holds the next letter

parts.note: Orion is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter S

explanation.surface: The constellation plays host at the start of a solemn prayer under the night sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Orison is an archaic, literary word for a prayer spoken to God.

clue.text: What can be a sweet Polish horse with a shed outside hotel

indicators.note: outside means the rubbing letters sit around the hotel letter

parts.note: to polish is to rub
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: shed means cast off, so the named letter is dropped

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A rider polishes a horse with a shed outside the hotel, perhaps for a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but means rub; 'a shed' is not a hut but a shed A, leaving ARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb stalks are cooked as a dessert, in crumbles and pies, so it can be a sweet.

clue.text: The first gag could be what unnerves performer

indicators.note: could be means the letters may be arranged into something else

explanation.surface: An opening joke could be the thing that rattles a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The three words supply all eleven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage fright is the nervous dread an actor feels before facing an audience.

clue.text: Bore put up contribution to ground rent

indicators.note: put up says the hidden letters are read backwards
contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tedious person has raised the payment towards the ground rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerd is a dull, socially awkward obsessive, the kind of person thought a bore.

clue.text: Finished training after Irish backs, past their best?

indicators.note: after places the training letters behind the reversed Irish ones

parts.note: a game that is finished is over

indicators.note: backs here means goes backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: PE, physical education, is physical training

explanation.surface: The Irish backs have finished their training session, and they are perhaps past their best.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture makes 'backs' look like players; it is the reversal signal turning IR into RI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is overripe has gone beyond its peak; the question mark flags applying it to the ageing players.

clue.text: A broadcast outside more costly: help from abroad found?

indicators.note: outside means the letters of A and AIR wrap round the costly piece

parts.note: to broadcast a programme is to air it
when prices are up, things are more costly

explanation.surface: A broadcast about soaring costs asks whether help from abroad can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more costly' is UP as in prices going up; 'broadcast' looks like it describes A but is its own piece, AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner who lives with a family and helps with childcare and housework.

clue.text: Mean sub: Connacht's right wing he hit

parts.note: sub as a prefix means below or under

indicators.note: the right wing of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Connacht, an Irish province, ends in T
to belt is to hit

explanation.surface: A rugby substitute from Connacht's right wing struck a nasty blow.
explanation.walkthrough: Connacht is the western province of Ireland, and has a rugby team; its right wing is its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: Below the belt describes an unfair, unsporting remark or action, which is a mean thing to do.

clue.text: Batting ruse team judge to be disrespectful

parts.note: in cricket the side batting is in
a con is a trick or ruse
a side is a team
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A batting side tries a sneaky trick on the umpire, which is thoroughly disrespectful.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the team batting is said to be 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inconsiderate means showing no thought or regard for others, which is a form of disrespect.

clue.text: Peacenik competent for part of term

parts.note: CO, conscientious objector, someone refusing to fight
efficient means competent and capable

explanation.surface: A capable pacifist stands in for part of the term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' looks like a school or legal term; it is an algebraic term such as 3x.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra a coefficient is the numerical factor multiplying a variable within a term.

clue.text: What mature people pay to import eastern lace?

indicators.note: to import is to bring in, so the eastern letter goes inside

parts.note: grown-ups pay the adult rate rather than a child's fare

explanation.surface: How much do grown-ups pay to bring in lace from the East?
explanation.walkthrough: 'lace' looks like the fabric; here it is the verb, as in lacing a drink with spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace a drink is to secretly add something to it, which is to adulterate or contaminate it.

clue.text: See about, say, dedicated lines

indicators.note: about means the see's letters go around the example abbreviation

parts.note: Ely in Cambridgeshire is a bishop's see, a cathedral city
EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Look at, for instance, some lines dedicated to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb; it is a bishop's diocese, here Ely.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a poem of mourning, verses written in memory of someone who has died.

clue.text: Belted clothing needed in the middle

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes and gear

indicators.note: only the central pair of letters of the word is taken

parts.note: the central letters of the word are E and D

explanation.surface: A belt was the bit of clothing needed round the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: Clobber is British slang for one's clothes or belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to hit them hard, so belted means struck or clobbered.

clue.text: Church of England admitting fine English cup's a drink dispenser

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the church abbreviation takes the next letters inside

parts.note: the Church of England is abbreviated C of E
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a sporting cup or trophy is a pot; the 's is a link meaning is

explanation.surface: The Church of England lets in a fine English cup as a drinks dispenser at the vicarage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffeepot is a vessel from which coffee is poured, so it dispenses a hot drink.

clue.text: Reported Thamessider's cultivated fuzz

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is judged by how it sounds

parts.note: cultivated means highbrow, and a Londoner from beside the Thames, imagined as a Cockney, drops the aitch to say 'IGHBROW

explanation.surface: A Londoner's cultivated fuzz was reported in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney speaker drops the H, so HIGHBROW said that way becomes 'IGHBROW, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebrow is a strip of short hairs above the eye, a bit of facial fuzz.

clue.text: Bread roll: start to bake a set

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter B
jelly sets or gels

explanation.surface: Instructions for a bread roll: begin baking a batch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread roll, boiled before baking.

clue.text: On odd occasions worry with beer manufactured here?

definitions.text: On odd occasions worry with beer manufactured here?

indicators.note: manufactured means made up, so the letters are rearranged
only the odd-numbered letters are taken: first, third and fifth

parts.note: odd letters W, R, Y

explanation.surface: A worried brewer wonders whether this is where beer gets made.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the place where beer is manufactured.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery is the factory where beer is brewed and produced commercially.

clue.text: A hundred troops send mad ambassador to get drink

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
to dement is an old verb meaning to drive mad
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A hundred soldiers drive a diplomat mad so he hits the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's corps of engineers; HE (His Excellency) is the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de menthe is a sweet, green, mint-flavoured liqueur served as an after-dinner drink.

clue.text: Ducks circle outskirts of small city

indicators.note: to circle is to surround, so the two O's go around the next letters

parts.note: a duck is a cricket score of nought, shaped O, so two ducks are OO

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: outer letters S and L

explanation.surface: Ducks swim in a circle on the edge of a small city.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: It keeps one blunder within range

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the sex-appeal letters enclose the rest

parts.note: it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
I is the Roman numeral for one
to err is to make a blunder

explanation.surface: Something holds a single error within its range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' for SA (sex appeal) is an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged mountain chain, in other words a mountain range.

clue.text: Greek division with gunners replicated spirit

parts.note: a deme was an administrative district in ancient Attica
RA, the Royal Artillery, are the gunners
replicated means the gunners' letters come a second time

explanation.surface: A Greek unit and some gunners duplicated their spirited efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: A deme was a local district of ancient Athens; the Royal Artillery's RA appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Demerara rum is a dark spirit distilled in Guyana, named after the Demerara river region.

clue.text: Put away articles husband left out

indicators.note: left out means omitted, so the husband letter is removed

parts.note: a and the are the English articles

explanation.surface: Someone tidied the items away, leaving the husband out.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is informal for eating it up, so ate fits as the past tense.

clue.text: Ring a power unit withdrawing capital

parts.note: a ring is O-shaped

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: A ring and a power unit being taken back from the capital's grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Gas is initially escaping your tip within hearing

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: first letter E

indicators.note: within hearing means as it would be heard, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: thy is old-fashioned your, and to tip is to lean

explanation.surface: Gas is leaking out, so tip your head within earshot.
explanation.walkthrough: THY LEAN said aloud gives the ending of the gas's name, after the E from 'escaping'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a colourless flammable hydrocarbon gas used to make plastics and ripen fruit.
